cohort: The study included 30 neonates, comprising 13 born to mothers with early-onset preeclampsia (preterm) and 17 healthy neonates (term).
finding: Changes in hemorheological parameters, especially RBC aggregation properties, suggest better microcirculation in preterm neonates at birth, potentially serving as an adaptation mechanism to impaired uteroplacental microcirculation in preeclampsia.
